name: Accordion
description: A set of sections, each opened by its own header. Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/

props.name: children
props.description: The sections: one `Accordion.Item` each, holding an `Accordion.Trigger` and an `Accordion.Panel`.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled: the values of every panel standing open. Leave it out and the widget owns them.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Which panels start open. Left out, all of them are closed.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the panels now open, in the order they were opened.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Whether several panels may stand open at once. Default `false`, so opening one closes the last.

props.name: loop
props.description: Whether Down and Up wrap around at the ends. Default `true`.

props.name: level
props.description: Which heading each header sits in. Default `3`. It has to fit the page around it — a heading level is the document's outline, and a screen reader navigates by it.

parts.name: Accordion.Item
parts.description: One section. It owns the pair of ids its header and its panel are wired together by.

props.name: value
props.description: What this section stands for, and what the widget reports when it is open.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Not openable, and stepped over by Down and Up. It is the `disabled` attribute, so the browser has already taken the header out of the tab sequence — arrows that still stopped there would be reaching what Tab cannot.

parts.name: Accordion.Trigger
parts.description: The header: a real `<button>` in a heading, which is the pair APG asks for.

props.name: level
props.description: This header's heading level, when it differs from the one the accordion sets.

props.name: arrow
props.description: Whether to draw the chevron. Turn it off to supply an affordance of your own. Default `true`.

parts.name: Accordion.Panel
parts.description: The section's content, in the grid that gives it its height.

keyboard.action: Every header is in the tab sequence, and so is anything inside an open panel. An accordion is not a composite widget, so nothing here is a roving tabindex.
Opens the header's panel, or closes it.
The next and previous header, wrapping at the ends and stepping over disabled ones. They do nothing inside a panel, so a textarea in one keeps its own arrows.

a11y: Each header is a `<button aria-expanded>` inside a heading — `level` says which, and it has to fit the outline of the page around it.
`aria-controls` on the header names its panel, which is always in the DOM, so the reference cannot dangle.
The panel is a `role="region"` named by its header. Pass `props={{ role: undefined }}` on a long accordion: past half a dozen panels the landmarks are noise, which is APG's own caveat.
The chevron is `aria-hidden`: it says what `aria-expanded` already says.
